newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent off on Iraq/German sales, sees support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent off on Iraq/German sales, sees support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures lost over half a dollar in active selling following news the U.N. and Iraq had agreed on aid plan details and on German plans to sell crude oil.
But the contract bounced off support and many felt the day's range had been seen.
Benchmark August Brent dropped 50 cents to $17.90 a barrel, having bounced off resistance at $17.85 a barrel.
"It's off on the Iraqi news and on German crude oil sales," one broker said.
"I think we have made the range. We are going to bounce off here. I think people are a little overreactive which is why we will bounce," another broker commented.
It was not immediately clear when the Iraqi oil sales would resume.

The U.N. co-ordinator in Baghdad, Staffan De Mistura, said the U.N. had finalised talks with Iraq on a food distribution plan. He said the text of the deal between Iraq and the U.N. on a food distribution plan needed to be finalised and translated into Arabic.
"We believe the whole process will be concluded by next Monday, including the official submission by the government of Iraq to the secretary-general of the United Nations," he said.

Confirmation by the German economics ministry that it would sell 2.8 million barrels of crude oil from strategic crude oil reserves in its first tender starting August 4 was also seen as bearish by the market.
August gas oil was off $1.25 a tonne at $160.75 following the news. The contract earlier traded to an intra-day high of $165.25 a tonne.
